s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on MRI
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
MRI showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with pathology findings of spindled cells and mature adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to spindle cell lipoma, with mixed fibrous and adipose tissue, and variable cell morphology

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the painful nature of the lesion, given its association with vascular components

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this entity cannot be entirely excluded without further evaluation, given its potential for pigmentation and subcutaneous involvement

raw.rationale: The pathology results, including mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells being spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, are consistent with Nora lesion. Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34, which also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: While spindle cell lipoma can have similar histological features, the presence of extensive pigment deposition and the specific immunohistochemical profile (strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A) are more characteristic of Nora lesion.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic lipoma typically has a distinct appearance with floret-like giant cells, which were not described in the pathology findings.

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: Angiolipoma is characterized by the presence of vascular proliferation within the lipoma, which was not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans typically has a more aggressive appearance with a storiform pattern and is usually positive for CD34, but the clinical presentation and other histological features do not match this diagnosis as closely as they match Nora lesion.
